title: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
intro: A widely used screening questionnaire for emotional wellbeing during pregnancy and after birth. It takes about three minutes. It is a screening, not a diagnosis.
question: Question {{current}} of {{total}}
saved: Your screening result has been saved.
shareNote: Consider sharing your result with your midwife, GP or health visitor. They can help you decide on next steps.
footer: Your feelings matter. You're not alone.

low.message: Your answers suggest few signs of depression right now. Keep prioritising rest, support and self-care, and check in again if things change.
low.chat: Talk with MumWell about staying well

mild.message: Your answers suggest some mood changes. Talking to people close to you, your midwife or GP can help, and it's worth repeating the screening in two weeks.

high.message: Your answers suggest you may be experiencing depression. Please contact your midwife, GP or health visitor soon for a proper assessment. Support really helps.

questions.q: I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things.
options: As much as I always could

questions.q: I have looked forward with enjoyment to things.
options: As much as I ever did
Rather less than I used to
Definitely less than I used to

questions.q: I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason.
I have felt scared or panicky for no good reason.
Things have been getting on top of me.
options: No, I have been coping as well as ever
No, most of the time I have coped quite well
Yes, sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual
Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all

questions.q: I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping.
I have felt sad or miserable.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying.

source: EPDS: Cox, J.L., Holden, J.M., & Sagovsky, R. (1987). British Journal of Psychiatry, 150, 782–786.
